decisions.decision: agree, with a bounded documentation qualification
decisions.basis: The ADR cleanly separates same-adapter repeatability (retained) from CPU/device and adapter identity (relaxed). Sampled tests directly assert repeatability on one/fresh Device and retained replay. Cross-lane and fixed-function comparisons either stay exact where measured or use explicit bounds. ADR0072's fixed-function bound is derived per pixel from store count and alpha rather than selected as a fixture-wide constant.
decisions.qualification: Do not describe the current set of passing exact shader-vs-mirror assertions as a cross-vendor contract. Conversely, do not silently allow an unmeasured divergence: record the pixel/rule/adapter and derive a numeric bound as ADR0082 requires. A future failure is actionable evidence for quantifying closeness, not automatically a production correctness defect.
decisions.unreviewed: No audit of every raster backend, adapter, scene family, or new GPU pass; no independent GPU execution performed in this shard.

decisions.decision: retain distinction; no separate test draft proposed
decisions.basis: Pixel-level bound comparisons can expose geometric displacement, but the fixed-function color bound is intentionally amplified by 1/alpha for straight-alpha conversion. The one-level glyph and shallow-edge lane tests discuss coverage/alpha explicitly, so they are not evidence for arbitrary geometric displacement or all color spaces.
decisions.qualification: The bound must not be summarized as a global per-channel color tolerance or as a geometric invariant. Existing per-pixel disagreement reports are the right place to detect a shift; an aggregate average or scene-wide maximum detached from store/alpha would lose that distinction.
